summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly integrated AI/ML capabilities, moving from simple in-database ML model training to full LLM orchestration, vector search, and embedding generation. By 2026, vector search has become a critical enterprise requirement with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on it, driving platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and MongoDB to build native vector capabilities. The competitive landscape spans purpose-built vector databases, extensions like pgvector, and fully integrated AI data clouds offering text-to-SQL, RAG pipelines, and model inference at query time.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of fully managed AI functions directly within the Snowflake platform, including LLM inference, text-to-SQL via Cortex Analyst, embedding generation, document processing via Cortex Search, and fine-tuning. Snowflake Postgres (generally available 2026) integrates natively with the AI Data Cloud and includes pgvector support for vector similarity search. Cortex AI eliminates the need to move data outside Snowflake for AI workloads, with governance and security inherited from the platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native vector search is available via Cortex Search, a fully managed retrieval service built into Snowflake. Additionally, Snowflake Postgres integrates pgvector as a native extension within the Snowflake environment, meaning vector search is treated as a first-class capability rather than an external add-on. Cortex Search handles chunking, embedding, and retrieval natively.
databases.llm_integration: Cortex AI supports hosted LLMs including Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others via COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, and TRANSLATE functions. Cortex Analyst provides natural language to SQL. External model integrations via Snowpark ML are also supported.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. LLM inference costs vary by model and token count. Cortex Search has separate indexing and query costs. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows compute and storage model. Overall costs depend on warehouse size and query volume.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to build and run ML models using standard SQL directly inside BigQuery, supporting logistic regression, boosted trees, matrix factorization, time series forecasting, and deep neural networks. BigQuery also integrates deeply with Vertex AI, enabling remote model inference against Vertex-hosted models and Gemini, embedding generation via the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function, and vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function introduced for GA. The platform supports multimodal embeddings and grounding LLM outputs with BigQuery data.
databases.vector_search_notes: BigQuery has native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH SQL function, which performs approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns stored directly in BigQuery tables. No external extension or separate infrastructure is required. It supports cosine, Euclidean, and dot product distance metrics natively.
databases.llm_integration: Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Flash, and others) are accessible via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions. Vertex AI hosted models including Anthropic Claude and third-party models are callable via remote model connections. BigQuery also supports Vertex AI Pipelines and AutoML integration.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and prediction are billed per byte processed or via flat-rate slots. Embedding generation and LLM inference via Vertex AI integration are billed separately per Vertex AI pricing (per 1K characters or tokens depending on model). VECTOR_SEARCH queries are billed as standard BigQuery query bytes scanned.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: PostgreSQL itself has no built-in AI features, but the open-source extension ecosystem makes it a highly capable AI-ready database. pgvector adds vector similarity search directly to Postgres instances with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing, enabling RAG pipelines without new infrastructure. pgai (by Timescale) extends this further by enabling embedding generation and LLM calls directly from SQL using OpenAI, Ollama, and other providers. For most teams in 2026, pgvector on Postgres is recommended as the best starting point for RAG workloads handling up to 50 million vectors.
databases.vector_search_notes: pgvector is an open-source extension that adds native vector search to PostgreSQL using HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. While it is an extension rather than a core built-in feature, it is so widely adopted and trivially installed (CREATE EXTENSION vector) that it is effectively the standard Postgres vector capability. It integrates with Snowflake Postgres, Supabase, AWS Aurora, and Timescale. For standalone open-source Postgres, this is the canonical vector search approach.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension enables direct SQL calls to OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, and Cohere APIs for embedding generation and LLM completion from within Postgres. Timescale's pgai Vectorizer automates embedding creation and synchronization. Snowflake Cortex provides text-to-SQL and embedding generation when running Snowflake Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are free open-source extensions. Costs depend entirely on the Postgres hosting environment (self-hosted, Supabase, Timescale Cloud, AWS RDS, etc.) and any external LLM API calls made via pgai. Managed Postgres services charge standard compute and storage rates.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables Aurora MySQL-Compatible and Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible databases to call Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock models directly from SQL queries using the aws_ml extension and built-in functions. This allows inference to run at query time without exporting data. Aurora ML is designed for use cases where predictions need to be embedded into transactional SQL workflows, such as scoring rows during a SELECT statement. It does not provide built-in ML model training within the database itself.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora does not have native built-in vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible supports pgvector as an installable extension, which adds vector similarity search capability. However, this is a third-party open-source extension, not a native Aurora feature. Aurora MySQL-Compatible does not support pgvector. For production vector workloads, pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL is common but should be understood as extension-based, not native.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock (Claude, Titan, Llama, Stable Diffusion, and others) and Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints via SQL functions. The aws_bedrock.invoke_model function allows calling any Bedrock-supported model directly from Aurora SQL. SageMaker Autopilot models can also be invoked via aws_sagemaker.invoke_endpoint.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference costs include standard Aurora compute costs plus per-invocation charges for SageMaker or Bedrock API calls. Bedrock pricing varies by model (per 1K input/output tokens). There is no additional charge for the Aurora ML integration itself beyond underlying service costs.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Amazon Redshift ML allows data analysts and engineers to create, train, and deploy ML models using simple SQL commands within Redshift, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot under the hood. Users run CREATE MODEL SQL statements and Redshift automatically exports data to S3, trains a model via SageMaker Autopilot, and makes the resulting model available as a SQL function for inference. Redshift ML also supports importing pre-trained SageMaker models and BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) scenarios. It is purpose-built for analytics workloads in a data warehouse context.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift does not have native built-in vector search. Amazon recently added support for storing and querying vectors in Redshift via APPROXIMATE NEAREST NEIGHBOR queries in preview, but as of mid-2026 this is not generally available as a fully native production feature comparable to purpose-built vector databases. For enterprise vector search workloads, Amazon OpenSearch Service or Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases are the recommended AWS-native alternatives.
databases.llm_integration: Redshift ML integrates with SageMaker Autopilot for automated model training. For LLM inference, Redshift can invoke SageMaker real-time endpoints including models deployed from Bedrock via the FUNCTION integration. Direct Bedrock model invocation from Redshift SQL is less native compared to Aurora ML; typically requires external Lambda or SageMaker endpoint intermediary.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML training costs include SageMaker Autopilot training job costs (billed per instance-hour) plus S3 data transfer and storage for exported training data. Inference via ML functions within Redshift queries does not incur additional per-query ML charges beyond the SageMaker endpoint hosting cost. Redshift Serverless or provisioned cluster costs apply for compute.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks offers a comprehensive AI platform under the Mosaic AI brand, encompassing model training (including LLM fine-tuning and pretraining via Mosaic AI Training), model serving via Model Serving endpoints, MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry, AI Playground for LLM experimentation, and Databricks Vector Search for retrieval-augmented generation. The platform integrates with Unity Catalog for governed AI assets. Databricks also provides AI BI (Genie) for natural language querying of data and supports Spark-based distributed ML workloads at scale.
databases.vector_search_notes: Databricks Vector Search is a native built-in vector database service fully integrated into the Databricks platform. It supports creating vector search indexes directly from Delta Lake tables with automatic sync, and querying via Python SDK or REST API. It uses Databricks-managed infrastructure with Unity Catalog governance. No external vector database infrastructure is required. It also integrates with pgvector-compatible workflows and Snowflake via mirroring.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving supports Foundation Model APIs (DBRX, Meta Llama, Mixtral) with pay-per-token pricing, external model endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI), and custom fine-tuned model deployment. Databricks AI Functions provide SQL-level LLM access via ai_query(). LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations are first-class supported.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks Vector Search is billed in Databricks Units (DBUs) based on the number of vector index units and query volume. Foundation Model API inference is billed per token (competitive with direct API pricing). Model training and fine-tuning are billed per GPU-hour via Databricks compute. Overall platform costs can be significant at scale but unified billing simplifies management.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search provides native vector similarity search integrated directly into the Atlas document database, enabling teams to store vector embeddings alongside their operational data in the same database rather than maintaining separate vector infrastructure. It supports Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search using HNSW indexes, hybrid search combining vector and full-text search, and pre-filtering by metadata fields. Atlas AI capabilities also include integration with major embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Amazon Bedrock for end-to-end RAG pipeline construction.
databases.vector_search_notes: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a fully native built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas, not an extension or third-party add-on. Vector indexes are created via the Atlas Search index configuration on any field containing array embeddings. It supports cosine similarity, dot product, and Euclidean distance. It handles filtering, hybrid search, and multi-vector queries natively within the MongoDB aggregation pipeline using the $vectorSearch stage.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Hugging Face, and Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation. Atlas AI includes connectors for LangChain, LlamaIndex, Spring AI, and Semantic Kernel. MongoDB also offers Atlas Stream Processing for real-time AI pipelines. There is no native hosted LLM within Atlas itself, but the platform is designed as the data layer for externally hosted models.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included with Atlas clusters at no additional base cost, but requires M10 or higher dedicated cluster tiers (M10 starts around $0.08/hour). Vector index storage and query compute are billed within standard Atlas pricing. Atlas Serverless supports vector search with per-operation billing. Costs scale with index size, number of dimensions, and query volume.
